skill.name: personwise-report-briefing
skill.description: Create grounded, interactive PersonWise briefing courses from supplied reports, whitepapers, and benchmark studies, including findings, methods, limitations, and audience questions.
skill.summary: Turn supplied reports into askable digital-human briefing courses.
skill.author: personwiseai

security_audit.summary: The 142 static alerts are false positives: documented backticks do not execute code, installer operations are bounded, and the encoded descriptor contains expected signed metadata. Three medium risks remain: third-party document upload, automatic use of existing course credits, and disabled native signature verification for Windows and macOS binaries. No prompt injection attempt or concealed executable payload was found.

remediation.issue: Selected source documents and images are uploaded to PersonWise.
remediation.suggestion: Show the destination and privacy impact before upload, and require explicit confirmation for confidential, regulated, or personally identifiable material.

remediation.issue: Course creation can consume existing credits without a separate confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Display the resolved course count and credit impact, then obtain explicit confirmation immediately before each metered course creation.

remediation.issue: Native signature verification is disabled for the bundled Windows and macOS release.
remediation.suggestion: Require valid Authenticode and Apple signing identities in addition to pinned hashes, and reject releases marked deferred or unsigned.

semantic_findings.title: Selected Documents Are Uploaded to a Third-Party Service
semantic_findings.description: The workflow uploads user-selected reports and images to PersonWise for processing. Sensitive documents therefore leave the local environment, even though discovered files require separate approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: SKILL.md directly instructs source upload with source add and permits selected images as references. The external transfer is an explicit part of the workflow.

semantic_findings.title: Course Creation Consumes Existing Credits Without Separate Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill treats a creation request as authorization to consume existing course credits and explicitly avoids another confirmation. Implicit invocation can therefore trigger metered account usage.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The authorization section explicitly permits existing-credit use without asking again, and the readiness section creates a durable run after checking the live allowance.

semantic_findings.title: Native Platform Signature Verification Is Disabled
semantic_findings.description: Windows and macOS installers accept pinned executable hashes while native signature requirements remain disabled. Hash pinning limits tampering but does not provide independent platform provenance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both installers set native signing to deferred or not required, making the Authenticode and macOS identity checks unreachable for the bundled release.

content.value_statement: Long reports are difficult to present accurately and invite limited audience interaction. This skill converts supplied sources into grounded, interactive PersonWise briefing courses.
actual_capabilities: Structures a briefing around findings, evidence, methods, limitations, discussion, and recall checks.
Creates PersonWise courses with designed slides, presenter scripts, and grounded audience questions.
Uploads user-selected reports and images as bounded course sources.
Reviews outline, script, image, and terminal checkpoints before delivery.
Applies targeted corrections through revision-aware course updates.
Supports private delivery, link access, and Topics submission when requested.
limitations: Requires a PersonWise account, browser OAuth, network access, and a compatible PersonWise CLI.
Course creation uses existing credits and follows live account page limits.
Does not perform original research or analyze raw datasets.
Cannot support claims, predictions, or recommendations beyond the supplied report.

use_cases.title: Brief Research Leadership
use_cases.description: Convert a whitepaper into an interactive executive briefing that preserves methods, caveats, and key evidence.

use_cases.title: Present Policy Findings
use_cases.description: Turn a policy report into a source-grounded presentation with clear limits and audience questions.

use_cases.title: Teach Benchmark Results
use_cases.description: Build a training course that explains benchmark findings and checks accurate recall.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Report Briefing
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a private interactive briefing from [report]. Focus on the main findings, method, and stated limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a faithful overview from one supplied report.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt the Briefing for an Audience
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [page count]-page briefing from [report] for [audience]. Emphasize [priority] while preserving all relevant caveats.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs a concise briefing tailored to a specific audience.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Findings Across Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a materials-only briefing from [reports]. Separate each source's findings, identify supported agreements, and preserve differences in method and scope.
prompt_templates.scenario: An analyst needs a grounded synthesis of several supplied documents.

prompt_templates.title: Build and Publish an Advanced Briefing
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [page count]-page interactive course from [sources] for [audience]. Review every checkpoint, correct unsupported claims, and publish with [access mode].
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced user needs reviewed production output with a defined access target.

output_examples.input: Create a private five-page briefing from our workforce benchmark report.
output_examples.output: A private five-page course covering the headline finding, evidence, method, limitations, and discussion. Delivery includes the login-required course link and verified source status.

output_examples.input: Turn two supplied policy reports into an interactive briefing for city leaders.
output: The course distinguishes findings from each report.
Shared conclusions appear only where both sources support them.
Methods, timeframes, and caveats remain attached to each claim.

output_examples.input: Publish our benchmark briefing for anyone with the link.
output_examples.output: The completed course uses link access and returns the verified public share link. The final report states the page count, source status, and review result.

best_practices: Supply the exact reports and identify the intended audience.
State the desired page count and access mode before creation.
Review sensitive documents before authorizing external upload.
anti_patterns: Do not request conclusions that the supplied sources cannot support.
Do not use this skill for original research or raw dataset analysis.
Do not describe a private editor link as a public share link.

faq.question: What source materials can I use?
faq.answer: You can use reports, whitepapers, benchmark studies, selected images, and clearly supplied text.

faq.question: Does the skill conduct new research?
faq.answer: No. It creates a briefing from supplied evidence and does not analyze raw datasets or invent new findings.

faq.question: Can the audience ask questions?
faq.answer: Yes. PersonWise courses support voice questions grounded in the course content.

faq.question: Does course creation use credits?
faq.answer: Yes. New courses use existing PersonWise credits and must fit current account limits.

faq.question: Are my documents uploaded?
faq.answer: Yes. Selected source documents and images are uploaded to PersonWise for course processing.

faq.question: Can I share the finished briefing?
faq.answer: Yes. Request link access for public sharing, or keep private access for authenticated viewing.
